Gene Description

CASP6 (caspase-6, formerly Mch2) is a short-prodomain apoptotic caspase and Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase. It is synthesized as an inactive zymogen and can be activated by processing by other caspases or by self-processing at its intersubunit linker, generating the large and small subunits of the active dimeric enzyme. CASP6 acts in cytosolic and nuclear apoptotic proteolysis, where it cleaves substrates including RIPK1, lamins, SATB1, vimentin, MAPT/tau, and, in hepatocyte NASH models, BID. Compared with CASP3 and CASP7 it has a narrower, partly nuclear executioner role and a distinctive ability to self-activate. CASP6 also has a non-catalytic innate-immune role during influenza A virus infection, binding RIPK3 and enhancing RIPK3-ZBP1 assembly to drive ZBP1-dependent inflammasome activation, pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis.

GO_REF:0000052 		UNDECIDED
Summary: The Human Protein Atlas places CASP6 in the fibrillar center, but the local cache has no image-level evidence and the curated CASP6 literature supports broader cytosolic/nuclear pools.
Reason: Fibrillar center is a precise nucleolar subcompartment; because the evidence is only the HPA GO_REF row and the local CASP6 literature does not independently support a fibrillar-center pool, retain this for human curator review.

Summary: CASP6 promotes innate immune activation during influenza A virus infection through a non-catalytic RIPK3/ZBP1 scaffolding role.

Summary: CASP6 has inherited apoptotic-caspase biology, but this top-level apoptotic-process row can be tightened to the execution phase.
Reason: The PTN000047947 PAINT node supports inherited apoptotic-caspase biology for CASP6; for human CASP6, direct substrate-cleavage evidence places its apoptotic protease work in the execution phase, while the separate RIPK1/BID rows capture intrinsic-signaling feedback contexts.

Core Functions

CASP6 is an Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase that cleaves protein substrates after VEHD/VEID-like caspase recognition sequences and can activate its own zymogen by intersubunit-linker self-processing at Asp-193/Asp-179.

Molecular Function:
cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
Directly Involved In:
protein autoprocessing
Cellular Locations:
cytosol nucleoplasm
Supporting Evidence:
  • file:human/CASP6/CASP6-uniprot.txt
    Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Val-Glu-His-Asp
  • PMID:7796396
    recombinant Mch2 alpha, but not Mch2 beta, possesses protease activity
  • PMID:19133298
    Casp6 was self-processed and activated in vitro and in vivo
  • PMID:20890311
    intramolecular cleavage at Asp 193 is a prerequisite for CASP6 self-activation

CASP6 carries out apoptotic substrate cleavage in intrinsic and executioner-caspase contexts, including RIPK1 cleavage downstream of cytochrome c/caspase-9 and cleavage of nuclear substrates such as lamins and SATB1.

Molecular Function:
cysteine-type endopeptidase activity
Directly Involved In:
execution phase of apoptosis intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
Cellular Locations:
cytosol nucleoplasm
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:22858542
    The only apoptotic caspase that cleaved more than 50% of total RIPK1 under these experimental conditions was the executioner caspase-6
  • PMID:18408014
    A SUMO-independent interaction of inactive caspase-6 and SATB1 was noted.
  • Reactome:R-HSA-352268
    Cleaved Satb1 dissociates from chromatin
  • PMID:32029622
    Active caspase-6 cleaved Bid to induce cytochrome c release, generating a feedforward loop that leads to hepatocyte death.

CASP6 acts as a non-catalytic adaptor in the ZBP1/RIPK3 cell-death complex during influenza A virus infection, increasing ZBP1-RIPK3 association to promote inflammasome activation, pyroptosis, apoptosis, necroptosis, and antiviral host defense.

Molecular Function:
molecular adaptor activity
Directly Involved In:
activation of innate immune response pyroptotic inflammatory response positive regulation of necroptotic process positive regulation of apoptotic process
Cellular Locations:
cytosol

    caspase-6 promotes the activation of programmed cell death pathways including pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis (PANoptosis)
  • PMID:32298652
    caspase-6 is able to enhance the interaction between ZBP1 and RIPK3

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Should GO add a child of molecular adaptor activity for caspase-mediated RHIM-complex scaffolding, and should CASP6-RIPK3-ZBP1 annotations use has_input extensions for RIPK3 and ZBP1?

Suggested experts: Kanneganti TD, Zheng M

Q: Does the Human Protein Atlas fibrillar-center signal reflect endogenous CASP6 localization, apoptotic relocalization, or antibody/background signal, and should this precise HPA component row be retained?

Q: Can the Caco-2 differentiation proteomics study be rechecked for CASP6 perturbation or follow-up evidence, or should the epithelial cell differentiation IEP row be removed as expression-only?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Introduce separation-of-function CASP6 truncations and IDR point mutants into CASP6-deficient macrophages and test endogenous RIPK3-ZBP1 co-immunoprecipitation, caspase-1 cleavage, MLKL phosphorylation, and cell death after influenza A virus infection.

Hypothesis: CASP6 bridges RIPK3 to ZBP1 through intrinsically disordered regions independently of its catalytic cysteine.

Type: structure-function rescue assay

Experiment: Perform N-terminomics in isogenic CASP6, CASP3, and CASP7 knockout cells undergoing cytochrome-c/etoposide-driven intrinsic apoptosis and compare endogenous cleavage of RIPK1, BID, lamins, SATB1, vimentin, and MAPT-like substrates.

Hypothesis: CASP6 cleaves a narrow, context-specific substrate set compared with CASP3/CASP7 during intrinsic apoptosis.

Type: degradomics / N-terminomics

CASP6 notes

2026-09-30

  • Re-audited the completed CASP6 review after refreshing GOA and UniProt. GOA
    still has the same 256 source rows and the YAML has no stale or missing rows.
    Tightened the two remaining broad GO:0006915 apoptotic-process assertions
    to GO:0097194 execution phase of apoptosis while keeping separate
    intrinsic-apoptotic-signaling and ZBP1/RIPK3 PANoptosis entries for the
    RIPK1/BID feedback and viral innate-immunity contexts.
  • Completed a manual CASP6 review from cached PubMed records, Reactome events,
    UniProt, GOA, the PTHR10454 PAINT context, and the existing
    Liver apoptosis regulation by CASP6 GO-CAM after provider-backed deep
    research was unavailable.
  • Accepted CASP6's core Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase activity,
    proteolytic self-activation, broad apoptotic role, RIPK1 cleavage in intrinsic
    apoptosis, and BID/hepatocyte and lamina/SATB1/vimentin substrate contexts as
    valid protease biology.
  • Added a conservative NEW GO:0060090 molecular adaptor activity assertion
    for the protease-independent RIPK3/ZBP1 scaffolding role in influenza
    A-induced PANoptosis, supported by PMID:32298652.
  • Removed 201 of 202 generic GO:0005515 protein binding rows and modified the
    SATB1 row to the informative CASP6 cysteine endopeptidase activity. Most
    removed rows came from the PMID:32814053 systematic yeast two-hybrid
    neurodegeneration interactome or other high-throughput interactome maps.
  • Treated several evidence gaps cautiously: the ATP11C/flippase cleavage row,
    the Caco-2 epithelial differentiation row, the HSP70/GATA1 cytosol row, and
    the Human Protein Atlas fibrillar-center localization row are UNDECIDED
    pending full-text, supplemental, or image-level confirmation.
  • Accepted the valid Reactome cytosol and nucleoplasm localization rows as
    core CASP6 compartment evidence. The remaining mixed-action warnings are
    intentional source-specific exceptions: an abstract-only ATP11C row, an
    abstract-only HSP70/GATA1 cytosol row, a TP53 expression event that projects
    CASP6 as product rather than actor, and a CAFA row from a DFF40/CAD paper
    without CASP6-specific evidence.
  • Marked the HIP14 palmitoylation row as MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED for CASP6
    because CASP6 is the inhibited target in that experiment, removed the TP53
    expression Reactome cytosol projection, and removed the CAFA staurosporine
    row from the DFF40/CAD paper because the cached full text contains no
    CASP6-specific evidence.

description: CASP6 (caspase-6, formerly Mch2) is a short-prodomain apoptotic caspase and Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase.
  It is synthesized as an inactive zymogen and can be activated by processing by other caspases or by self-processing at its
  intersubunit linker, generating the large and small subunits of the active dimeric enzyme. CASP6 acts in cytosolic and nuclear
  apoptotic proteolysis, where it cleaves substrates including RIPK1, lamins, SATB1, vimentin, MAPT/tau, and, in hepatocyte
  NASH models, BID. Compared with CASP3 and CASP7 it has a narrower, partly nuclear executioner role and a distinctive ability
  to self-activate. CASP6 also has a non-catalytic innate-immune role during influenza A virus infection, binding RIPK3 and
  enhancing RIPK3-ZBP1 assembly to drive ZBP1-dependent inflammasome activation, pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis.

- term:
    id: GO:0005654
    label: nucleoplasm
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000052
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: The Human Protein Atlas nucleoplasm call is consistent with Reactome-curated nuclear CASP6 translocation and
      substrate cleavage.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: Unlike the more precise fibrillar-center call, nucleoplasm agrees with curated CASP6 nuclear translocation and
      cleavage of nuclear substrates such as lamins and SATB1.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: Reactome:R-HSA-9029690
      supporting_text: Activated caspase-6 translocates to the nucleus
- term:
    id: GO:0005654
    label: nucleoplasm
  evidence_type: TAS
  original_reference_id: Reactome:R-HSA-264865
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: Reactome places active CASP6 in the nucleoplasm for nuclear substrate cleavage or nuclear translocation.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: Lamin A cleavage, Lamin B1 cleavage, SATB1 cleavage, and CASP6 nuclear-translocation events validly place active
      CASP6 in the nucleoplasm during apoptotic execution, one of the compartments of its core protease activity.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: Reactome:R-HSA-264865
      supporting_text: Lamin A is cleaved by active caspase 6

- term:
    id: GO:0005829
    label: cytosol
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000052
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: CASP6 has a cytosolic pool that participates in apoptotic and innate-immune signaling.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: Cytosolic CASP6 is consistent with its intrinsic-apoptosis RIPK1 cleavage and its ZBP1/RIPK3 role; the Reactome
      vimentin and translocation events are valid but only localization support.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:22858542
      supporting_text: The only apoptotic caspase that cleaved more than 50% of total RIPK1 under these experimental conditions
        was the executioner caspase-6

  review:
    summary: The TP53 expression event is about p53 stimulating CASP6 transcription, not an active CASP6 cytosolic reaction.

  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:12888622

  review:
    summary: CASP6 performs protein proteolysis through its cysteine-type endopeptidase activity.

    reason: Proteolysis is correct for CASP6 but is a broad biological-process parent relative to the more informative substrate-specific
      apoptotic cleavage events and autoprocessing activity.

      execution phase.

      substrate-cleavage evidence places its apoptotic protease work in the execution phase, while the separate RIPK1/BID
      rows capture intrinsic-signaling feedback contexts.

  review:
    summary: Active CASP6 is a dimer/tetrameric caspase, so identical-protein binding is biochemically plausible but not a

core_functions:
- description: CASP6 is an Asp-directed cysteine endopeptidase that cleaves protein substrates after VEHD/VEID-like caspase
    recognition sequences and can activate its own zymogen by intersubunit-linker self-processing at Asp-193/Asp-179.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004197

suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: CASP6 bridges RIPK3 to ZBP1 through intrinsically disordered regions independently of its catalytic cysteine.
  description: Introduce separation-of-function CASP6 truncations and IDR point mutants into CASP6-deficient macrophages and
    test endogenous RIPK3-ZBP1 co-immunoprecipitation, caspase-1 cleavage, MLKL phosphorylation, and cell death after influenza
    A virus infection.
  experiment_type: structure-function rescue assay
- hypothesis: CASP6 cleaves a narrow, context-specific substrate set compared with CASP3/CASP7 during intrinsic apoptosis.
  description: Perform N-terminomics in isogenic CASP6, CASP3, and CASP7 knockout cells undergoing cytochrome-c/etoposide-driven
    intrinsic apoptosis and compare endogenous cleavage of RIPK1, BID, lamins, SATB1, vimentin, and MAPT-like substrates.
  experiment_type: degradomics / N-terminomics
